title: Observability module orchestrator: opinionated Terraform wrapper for Prometheus/Grafana + OTEL + logs
creator: Aisha Kapoor
description:
Goal: provide a single, opinionated Terraform module that deploys and upgrades the full observability stack for VPC/private deployments (Prometheus + Grafana, OpenTelemetry Collector, and log shipping agents) with built-in health checks, automated canary upgrades, and safe rollback hooks. The module should be easy to consume for Private customers while preserving our operational controls and upgrade guarantees.

Scope and responsibilities:
- Terraform module API: clearly typed variables to configure Helm chart values, namespace, resource sizing profiles (dev/staging/prod), retention, remote_write endpoints, and log sink targets (S3/Vector/Fluentd).
- Deployment surface: helm_release (Prometheus/Grafana), k8s deployment/daemonset for OTEL collector and log shipping (Vector/Fluent Bit), and Kubernetes ServiceMonitors /PodMonitors where applicable.
- Upgrade orchestration: support staged canary upgrades using a) canary namespace or canary release naming, b) pre-upgrade validation jobs (k8s Job created via Helm hook or Terraform null_resource), c) automated Prometheus queries to validate metric ingestion and scrape stability post-upgrade, and d) automatic rollback trigger that runs helm rollback and flips TF-managed canary flag.
- Health checks & validation: comprehensive probes that include: scrape success rate (>99% for core targets), new metrics presence (expected metric names list), alert rules dry-run to detect rule compilation errors, and log throughput sanity checks (matching ingestion rates to baseline). All checks exposed as terraform data or outputs so CI workflows can gate applies.
- Safe defaults & profiles: small/medium/large profiles with conservative resource requests, PVC sizing for TSDB, and retention presets to avoid OOMs on smaller clusters.
- Upgrade hooks & self-heal: an opinionated null_resource/local-exec and remote-run pattern used for post-apply validation with idempotent runbooks and documented rollback steps. Module will create lightweight runner Jobs to run integration checks as part of the upgrade.
- Observability of the observability-stack: module exposes Kibana/Grafana endpoints (ingress annotations), Prometheus query endpoints, and a metrics dashboard template for tenant-level SLOs so customers can verify after upgrades.

Trade-offs and decisions considered:
- Sidecar vs daemonset for log shipping: daemonset chosen by default for cluster-wide efficiency; offer sidecar toggle for pod-level guarantees when customers want per-pod routing.
- Helm vs pure kubernetes manifests: Helm retained for chart upgrades and upstream compatibility; Terraform Helm provider will be the primary control surface but we will keep manifests templated for situations where Helm is blocked.
- Tight defaults vs configurability: provide opinionated safe defaults but allow override of core options; restrict dangerous knobs behind explicitly named variables (eg. enable_force_upgrade).

Testing and CI:
- Integration tests using Terratest in a disposable cluster that runs the full module and validates: Prometheus targets, OTEL ingestion, log lines appearance in sink, Grafana dashboards import. Test harness located at: https://github.com/redwood-inference/infra-tests/pulls/214
- GitHub Actions workflow gates: plan -> apply-canary -> run-validation -> promote-or-rollback. Workflow draft: https://github.com/redwood-inference/infra/.github/actions/workflows/observability-upgrade.yml

Docs and artifacts:
- Design doc with diagrams and upgrade sequence: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/INF/Opinionated+Observability+Terraform+Module
- Runbook for failed upgrade scenarios and manual rollback: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/INF/Obs+Upgrade+Runbook
- Dashboard template: https://grafana.redwood.ai/d/observability-stack/observability-overview

Acceptance criteria (MUST):
1) Module applies cleanly in a fresh namespace and creates Prometheus, Grafana, OTEL collector, and log shipping with profile=small.
2) Canary upgrade workflow can be executed from CI and performs at least 3 validation checks (scrape rate, metric presence, log ingestion).
3) On failing validation, automatic rollback completes and TF state returns to prior stable release.
4) Documentation for variables, example root module usage, and runbook are present in the module README.
5) Module passes the Terratest suite and GitHub Actions gate in staging.

Open questions / follow-ups:
- Do we require tenant-level encryption keys (KMS) for TSDB snapshots by default? This affects the module's IAM role requirements.
- Should we include Alertmanager as part of the module or keep it as an optional sibling module?

Links to related tickets and context:
- Observability TF foundations and previous modules: ENG-61234, ENG-76123
- Incident notes that motivated upgrade validation: https://docs.internal.redwood.ai/incidents/2025-11-prometheus-oom (summary included in design doc)

Next steps:
- Finalize variable schema and default profiles (this week).
- Implement canary release naming and pre/post hooks (next sprint).
- Wire up CI workflow and Terratest harness (in-parallel with implementation).
